name: abs_sub_round
result.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} [inst : Field α] [inst_1 : LinearOrder α] [IsStrictOrderedRing α] [inst_3 : FloorRing α] (x : α),
  |x - ↑(round x)| ≤ 1 / 2
result.value:
:= by
  rw [round_eq, abs_sub_le_iff]
  have := floor_le (x + 1 / 2)
  have := lt_floor_add_one (x + 1 / 2)
  constructor <;> linarith
result.informal_description: For any element $x$ in a linearly ordered ring $\alpha$, the absolute value of the difference between $x$ and its rounded value is at most $\frac{1}{2}$, i.e., $|x - \text{round}(x)| \leq \frac{1}{2}$.

result.informal_name: Fractional Part Lies in Unit Interval
result.informal_description: For any real number $ x $, the fractional part of $ x $, defined as $ x - \lfloor x \rfloor $, lies within the closed unit interval $[0, 1]$.

name: round
result.type: {α : Type u_2} → [inst : Ring α] → [inst_1 : LinearOrder α] → [FloorRing α] → α → ℤ
result.informal_name: Rounding function to nearest integer in a linearly ordered ring
result.informal_description: The function maps each element $ x $ of a linearly ordered ring $ \alpha $ to the nearest integer. Specifically, if the fractional part of $ x $ is less than $ \frac{1}{2} $, it returns the floor of $ x $; otherwise, it returns the ceiling of $ x $.

name: round_eq_iff
result.signature: {x : α} {n : ℤ} : round x = n ↔ x ∈ Ico (n - 1 / 2 : α) (n + 1 / 2)
result.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} [inst : Field α] [inst_1 : LinearOrder α] [IsStrictOrderedRing α] [inst_3 : FloorRing α] {x : α}
  {n : ℤ}, round x = n ↔ x ∈ Set.Ico (↑n - 1 / 2) (↑n + 1 / 2)
result.informal_name: Rounding Equals Integer iff in Interval
result.informal_description: For any element $x$ in a linearly ordered ring $\alpha$ and integer $n$, the rounding of $x$ to the nearest integer equals $n$ if and only if $x$ lies in the interval $\left[n - \frac{1}{2}, n + \frac{1}{2}\right)$.

name: abs_sub_round_eq_min
result.signature: (x : α) : |x - round x| = min (fract x) (1 - fract x)

  |x - ↑(round x)| = min (Int.fract x) (1 - Int.fract x)

result.informal_name: Absolute Difference Between x and Rounded x Equals Minimum of Fractional Part and Complement
result.informal_description: For any element $x$ in a linearly ordered ring $\alpha$, the absolute value of the difference between $x$ and its rounded value satisfies $|x - \text{round}(x)| = \min(\text{fract}(x), 1 - \text{fract}(x))$, where $\text{fract}(x) = x - \lfloor x \rfloor$ denotes the fractional part of $x$.
